subject: Cloud Computing
title: Bulkhead Isolation
description: A quick win: understand Bulkhead Isolation.

hook.text: A ship has watertight compartments. If one floods, the rest stay dry. Cloud systems need the same design.

buildup.text: Bulkhead isolation separates components so a failure in one doesn't bring down the others.

discovery.text: In practice: separate thread pools, separate databases, and separate scaling for critical vs. non-critical services.

twist.text: Isolation costs more. Running separate resources for each component means paying for duplicate infrastructure.

climax.text: The trade-off is worth it. When a non-critical feature fails, your payments and core services keep running.

punchline.text: Isolate the critical from the optional. Let non-essentials fail alone.

quiz.question: What does bulkhead isolation prevent in cloud systems?
options: A failure in one component from cascading and bringing down the entire system
Users from accessing services during maintenance windows
Data from being replicated across multiple regions

details.summary: Bulkhead isolation partitions system resources so that a failure in one component cannot exhaust resources needed by others. Named after ship bulkheads that prevent flooding from sinking the entire vessel, this pattern limits the blast radius of failures.
details.whyItMatters: Without isolation, a single runaway service or traffic spike can consume all available threads, connections, or memory, bringing down unrelated services sharing those resources.
takeaways: Resources are partitioned to limit failure blast radius
Named after ship compartments that contain flooding
Prevents one failing component from draining shared resources

faq.question: How is the bulkhead pattern implemented?
faq.answer: Common implementations include separate thread pools for different service calls, dedicated connection pools per dependency, and separate container or pod deployments for critical components. Each partition can fail without affecting others.

faq.question: How does bulkhead differ from circuit breaker?
faq.answer: Bulkhead prevents resource exhaustion by partitioning resources in advance. Circuit breaker detects failures and stops calling a broken service. They complement each other: bulkheads limit damage while circuit breakers stop the bleeding.
